subject: china-studies
title: Urbanisation: One Chinese City Changes Across the Decades
objectives: Explain urbanisation as a gradual process driven by people moving in, stage by stage
Read the urban and rural shares at each stage: urban 15, 38, 62, 85 and rural 85, 62, 38, 15 of every 100 people
Explain why two photographs decades apart do not show a single sudden change

definitions.meaning: The process by which a place becomes more urban over time: built-up districts grow and the share of people living in them climbs.
The number of every 100 people who live in built-up urban districts; in the animation it climbs 15 to 38 to 62 to 85.
The number of every 100 people who live and work in the countryside; it falls 85 to 62 to 38 to 15 as the urban share climbs.
The land covered by factories, housing and districts; it spreads outward stage by stage from the town core and the factories.
The fields around the town at the start; factories and housing are built on it at the edge stage by stage until only a remnant is left.
People moving in from the countryside for the factory jobs; their arrival drives each stage of building.

mechanismSteps: Farmland and a small town: the map is mostly farmland, a small town stands where the roads cross, and the urban share is 15 with the rural share at 85 (s1).
Factories and first housing appear: factories are built on farmland at the edge, their jobs pull people in, the first housing blocks rise beside them, and the urban share climbs to 38 (s2).

Built-up districts spread outward: the districts spread from the core and the factories, the farmland shrinks to a strip in the west, and the urban share reaches 62 while the rural share falls to 38 (s3).

A mostly built-up city, reached in stages: the urban share is 85 and only a farmland remnant is left, and replaying the stages corrects the sudden-leap version by showing the growth step by step (s4).
workedExample: Work through the whole growth in order. Start (s1): farmland and a small town, urban share 15, rural share 85. Stage 2 (s2): factories built on farmland at the edge pull migrants in for jobs, the first housing blocks rise, and the urban share climbs to 38. Stage 3 (s3): the built-up districts spread outward, the farmland shrinks to a western strip, and the urban share reaches 62 while the rural share falls to 38. Stage 4 (s4): the city is mostly built-up, urban share 85, rural share 15, with only a farmland remnant left. At every stage the order is the same: people move in for jobs, building follows them onto the farmland at the edge, and both shares move one stage at a time.

trap.misconception: A Chinese city becomes urban in one sudden leap, because its farmland is replaced by built-up districts all at once.
trap.explanation: The slip: Photographs of the same city decades apart look completely different, so it is easy to imagine the farmland was swept away and the city put in its place in a single step. The fix: Urbanisation is gradual and driven by people moving in: factories and the first housing blocks are built on farmland at the edge as migrants arrive for jobs, the built-up districts then spread outward stage by stage, and the urban population share climbs - and the rural share falls - at every stage until the city is mostly built-up. In class, replay scene 4: freeze on the sudden-leap version where the farmland is replaced all at once, then run the staged replay and ask what was built - and who moved in - at each stage as the urban share climbs.
